intro: Chopin’s Raindrop Prelude in D♭ major, Op. 28 No. 15, marked Sostenuto, repeats A♭ beneath the melody, and in the C♯ minor middle section the note is written as G♯. Ivan Ilić plays it in a recording made in Paris in October 2005.

sections.label: A · D♭ major melody over repeated A♭
sections.mNote: Repeated quavers under a slow right-hand melody.

sections.label: B · C♯ minor, repeated G♯ over chords
sections.mNote: The repeated note moves to the right hand.

sections.label: A′ · D♭ major melody, shortened
sections.mNote: The opening melody comes back in shortened form.

cues.title: Repeated A♭, opening bars
cues.text: The right hand plays a sustained melody in D♭ major over repeated A♭ quavers. The chords change around the repeated note. Chopin marks the piece Sostenuto.
cues.evidence: Breitkopf & Härtel first edition, bars 1–4: Sostenuto, recurring A♭ quavers and sustained right-hand melody. https://chopinscores.org/partytura/128
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: George Sand’s account, Valldemossa
cues.text: At Valldemossa, George Sand returned from Palma through heavy rain and found Chopin distraught at the piano. In her memoir, Histoire de ma vie, she wrote that he had dreamt of drowning, with icy drops falling on his chest. When she pointed to the rain on the roof, he angrily rejected the comparison.
cues.evidence: George Sand’s Histoire de ma vie, account of the Mallorca winter of 1838–39, quoted at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prelude,_Op._28,_No._15_(Chopin). Her memoir leaves the prelude unnamed; later tradition attaches the episode to No. 15. Mieczysław Tomaszewski discusses the rain association: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/208

cues.title: Change to C♯ minor
cues.text: The A♭ is now written G♯, on the same piano key. The right hand repeats it while the left hand plays the melody in low chords. D♭ major has moved to C♯ minor, and Chopin marks the new passage sotto voce, under the breath.
cues.evidence: Breitkopf & Härtel first edition, bars 27–31: change of key signature, right-hand G♯ quavers and lower left-hand melody, marked sotto voce. https://chopinscores.org/partytura/128
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Return of the opening melody
cues.text: The opening melody returns at bar 76, beginning on F above D♭, with the original key signature restored. The repeated A♭ sounds beneath the tune again. This return is brief and leads to a shortened close.
cues.evidence: Breitkopf & Härtel first edition, bars 75–83: return to the original key signature and opening melody at bar 76, followed by the abbreviated close. https://chopinscores.org/partytura/128
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Unaccompanied melody before the close
cues.text: Near the end, the left hand stops for two bars, and the melody descends alone in crotchets. The repeated A♭ returns beneath the closing chords. The prelude ends on a D♭ major chord.
cues.evidence: Breitkopf & Härtel first edition, bars 82–89: two bars of unaccompanied melody, then the repeated A♭ and final D♭-major chord. https://chopinscores.org/partytura/128
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: A♭ becomes G♯
transitions.from: A · D♭ major melody over repeated A♭
transitions.to: B · C♯ minor, repeated G♯ over chords
transitions.how: The opening melody stops, and A♭ continues alone in quavers. At bars 27–28 the key signature changes to C♯ minor, and the right hand writes the same sounding note as G♯. Low C♯ and G♯ begin the left-hand phrase, and E♮ soon adds the minor third. Chopin marks the passage sotto voce.
transitions.evidence: Breitkopf & Härtel first edition, bars 27–28. https://chopinscores.org/partytura/128

transitions.title: Return of the opening melody
transitions.from: B · C♯ minor, repeated G♯ over chords
transitions.how: The last hushed chords rest on a low G♯ in the bass. In the linking half-bar G♯ is respelt as A♭, and the left hand moves through F, G♭ and E♭. A D♭ bass then brings back the opening melody on F, marked piano, with the repeated quavers again beneath the tune.
transitions.evidence: Breitkopf & Härtel first edition, bars 74–76. https://chopinscores.org/partytura/128

composer.born: 1 March 1810, Żelazowa Wola, Duchy of Warsaw
composer.epithet: Composer for the piano, known for music that drew on operatic singing and on the irregular accents of the mazurka.
facts: Wojciech Żywny; composition with Józef Elsner in Warsaw, 1826–29
Warsaw · Paris from 1831 · summers at Nohant
Piano lessons, publishing and occasional concerts
The piano, from a few lines of mazurka to concertos and sonatas
composer.background:
In February 1832 Chopin, a twenty-one-year-old Polish pianist, played in the Pleyel rooms in Paris. He had arrived the previous autumn, with two concertos behind him. The concert caught the attention of the city’s publishers, and teaching soon supplied his living. For the rest of his life his profession depended on people hearing him at close quarters. The great public virtuosos travelled from one concert city to the next; Chopin stayed in Paris and gave lessons.

He was born at Żelazowa Wola in 1810. His father, Nicolas, had come from France and worked as a tutor; his mother, Justyna Krzyżanowska, was Polish. The family moved to Warsaw while Fryderyk was still a baby, when Nicolas obtained a teaching post at the Lyceum. At seven the boy had a polonaise in print. Wojciech Żywny taught him the piano, with Bach and Mozart among his models; Józef Elsner later gave him a rigorous training in composition at Warsaw’s Main School of Music.
